title: Evolution experiment record (version 1, frozen)
description: The experiment shape this repository shipped before a promotion recorded the merge unit it went as. A version-1 record that ended `promoted` states its promotion revision and no merge unit — not because a field is missing, but because the operation that wrote it recorded none — so the merge unit such a promotion went as is read from the batch outcome and held to the run that measured it. This file is never tightened: it exists so those records keep a defined read path. New records are written at the current version, and any operation that rewrites one writes it at that version.

experiment_id.description: `<batch-id>-exp-<NN>`, one past the highest ordinal its batch has ever used. Never reused: a historical experiment's name has to keep naming the attempt it was. The ordinal is a positive number zero-padded to two digits and no wider than it needs to be, so one attempt has exactly one spelling — `00` names no attempt, and `01` and `001` would be two directories for one position in the series. The batch's ordinals run 1..N with none missing and only the newest still open, which the controller enforces across the records the way the schema enforces the spelling of each.

base_revision.description: The exact source commit this experiment starts from, frozen by the batch's first experiment. Every experiment of one batch carries the same value; a differing one is refused rather than reconciled (contract invariant 15).

base_release_ref.description: The most recent release tag reachable from `base_revision` at creation time, or null when the checkout had none. Recorded rather than re-derived so the record still states which released protocol this candidate builds on after the tag is gone (contract invariant 4 keeps missing fields explicit).

ref.description: The durable Git ref holding this experiment's rounds. Fast-forward only, so every pinned candidate revision stays reachable after the working branch is deleted.

rounds.description: Append-only. At most one round is unsealed, and it is the last one; every earlier round is candidate-ready and is never edited again.

round.description: One revision pass: the tasks admitted into it and the candidate it produced. Replay evidence names a round, so sealing one and opening the next is what makes prior evidence stale by construction.

reason.description: Why this round exists — the grouped admission for round 1, the revision reason afterwards.

seal.description: What makes a round candidate-ready, or null while it is still taking work. One object rather than two nullable fields so a half-pinned round — sealed with no revision, or a revision nobody sealed — is not a shape this contract can even hold (contract invariant 16). Nothing measures an unsealed round: the tip moves while a round is open, so evidence gathered before this record exists cannot say which tree it described.

sealed_at.description: When the controller sealed the round, having observed every admitted task complete. Not when the last task finished.

candidate_revision.description: The ref tip pinned at that moment: the revision replay exercises and every terminal decision names. Immutable, and the ref stays here until a new round is opened. Distinct from the promotion revision a promoted candidate later produces on the source line.

admitted_task.description: One draft's admission: which proposal it was, the bytes admitted, the task the copy took, and whether that task was seen through to completion. The hash is the provenance a copied draft would otherwise lose the moment either file is edited.

draft_id.description: The draft's stem under `batches/<batch-id>/proposed-tasks/`. A kebab slug, so it is one path segment with no traversal, no dot-file, and no extension to confuse for one. A draft may be consumed once; re-proposing the idea means a new id.

completion_observed_at.description: When this task was observed at `completed`, or null while it has not been. Recorded here because the observation is the only durable form of it: `.ai-tasks/` is machine-local and close-out archives a finished task away, so on any other clone the task's own status is unreadable rather than merely absent. A round is sealed only once every task it admitted carries this (contract invariant 16).

decision.description: The terminal decision, or null while the experiment is open. `superseded_by` is set only for `superseded` and `promotion_revision` only for `promoted`; both are present and null otherwise. `promoted` additionally requires the last round to be candidate-ready, since what was promoted is the revision that round pinned and not the tip as it stood at decision time; `abandoned` and `superseded` may end an experiment whose last round was never sealed, which is the honest record of an attempt dropped before it produced a candidate. The controller enforces all of that, which the implemented JSON Schema subset cannot express — the fields stay explicit rather than optional so a record never leaves the reader guessing whether a value is absent or unrecorded.

superseded_by.description: The experiment that replaced this one: the same batch, the same base, and the next ordinal in the series, because superseding creates its successor in the same operation. The controller refuses any other name — an earlier attempt, a record's own id, or one that does not exist — since none of them is a replacement it could have made.

promotion_revision.description: The source-line commit carrying this candidate's change. Never the candidate tip it came from.
